Definition: from G4920; a mental putting together, i.e. intelligence or (concretely) the intellect:--knowledge, understanding.
BiblicalUsage: All who hear the boy Jesus in the temple are astonished at His understanding and answers, and the scribe agrees that loving God with all the heart and with all the understanding is more than all burnt offerings and sacrifices. Paul prays that the Colossians would be filled with the knowledge of God's will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding, and he tells Timothy to consider what he says, for the Lord will give him understanding in all things.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that understanding is a gift the Lord gives to those who consider His word, and I hold that loving God with my mind is worship, not only study. My position is plain: understanding that does not lead to love has missed its point.
